title: Python Input and Conversion
description: Handle text from input and convert it deliberately before doing numeric work.

questions.prompt: What type does input() return before conversion?
questions.explanation: Keyboard input arrives as text, even when the student types digits.
int converts the text 12 into the integer 12 before addition.
Both operands are strings, so + concatenates them rather than adding numeric values.

questions.prompt: Which conversion is appropriate for the text '3.5'?
questions.explanation: float accepts a decimal representation. int('3.5') raises ValueError because it is not whole-number text.
Each string is converted to an integer before the values are added.
The text has the wrong value format for integer conversion, so Python raises ValueError.

questions.prompt: Calling input('Name: ') displays the prompt before waiting for the answer.
questions.explanation: The string argument is shown to the user, then input waits for text.
str converts the integer to text so it can be joined with the other string.

questions.prompt: What is a safe design for functions used by automated tests?
options: Print the answer instead of returning it
Depend on a fixed prompt for every call
questions.explanation: Argument-based functions are deterministic and testable; interactive prompts belong in a user-facing main flow.
strip removes the leading and trailing spaces from the text.
